document: Social Security card (the de facto national ID)

routes.label: registration at a Social Security Board office

note: Belize's E-Governance chief, as Greater Belize reported, calls the Social Security card the de facto national ID (a biometric national ID is being piloted, not modelled). The Social Security Board's fees: a first card BZD 5 for a Belizean, BZD 26 for a replacement (not modelled); a parent applies for a child under 14. Under the Board's policy as News 5 reported it, a card issued to someone 14 or over doesn't expire; a younger child's card's term isn't stated. The time isn't stated.

sources.title: Greater Belize Media, on the national ID consultation (E-Governance CEO José Urbina)
sources.said: I can say today that the Social Security card has been adopted as the de facto national ID.

sources.title: Social Security Board (Belize), Registration Documents
sources.said: A parent or legal guardian must apply for the registration of a dependent child under the age of 14. ... First Issue $5.00 BZD Born Belizean, Naturalized Belizean, Permanent Resident of Belize ... Replacement $26.00BZD All replacement cards after first issue.

sources.title: News 5 Belize, SSB Card Won't Expire
sources.said: cards issued to persons fourteen years and over will not expire.
